title: Efficacy and safety of exercise training in patients with chronic heart failure: HF-ACTION randomized controlled trial
authors: O'Connor CM, Whellan DJ, Lee KL, Keteyian SJ, Cooper LS, Ellis SJ, et al.; HF-ACTION Investigators
population: Medically stable outpatients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (median 25%) at 82 centres in the United States, Canada and France, randomised April 2003 to February 2007; median age 59 years, 28% women, 37% in NYHA class III or IV
funder: Funded by 13 National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute grants (5U01HL063747 and others). The NHLBI had a role in the design and conduct of the study; in the collection, analysis and interpretation of the data; and in the preparation, review and approval of the manuscript.
result: Usual care plus aerobic exercise training (36 supervised sessions, then home-based training) against usual care alone. All-cause mortality or hospitalisation: 759 (65%) against 796 (68%), hazard ratio 0.93 (95% CI 0.84 to 1.02), P = 0.13; mortality 189 (16%) against 198 (17%), 0.96 (0.79 to 1.17); cardiovascular mortality or heart failure hospitalisation 344 (30%) against 393 (34%), 0.87 (0.75 to 1.00). In prespecified analyses adjusted for prognostic baseline characteristics, hazard ratios were 0.89 (0.81 to 0.99) for all-cause mortality or hospitalisation and 0.85 (0.74 to 0.99) for cardiovascular mortality or heart failure hospitalisation. Exercise adherence fell from a median 95 to 74 minutes a week between months 4 to 6 and 10 to 12; other adverse events were similar.
